arrestPower.summary: Arrest, process and bail are read from the CPC 2010 First Schedule entry for each Penal Code section.

s.18(1): any police officer may arrest without warrant any person offending in the officer's view against any provision of the Act. s.18(2): may also arrest without warrant a person reasonably suspected of a s.10(1) offence in the circumstances prescribed by regulations.

name: Miscellaneous Offences (Public Order and Nuisance) Act 1906

arrestPower.summary: s.40(1): any police officer may arrest without warrant any person offending in the officer's view against any provision of the Act. Also: s.22 offences are deemed arrestable (s.22(2)); any person may arrest anyone found offending against Part 4 (vagrancy, ss.26–27A) (s.28); Part 5 touting offences (s.34) and Part 6A SIM-card offences (s.39I) are deemed arrestable.

name: Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958

arrestPower.summary: Offences under ss.6, 7 and 8 are expressly arrestable and non-bailable. Other offences follow the CPC term default.

name: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act 2021
aliases: Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act

arrestPower.summary: Every offence under Part 2 is arrestable for the CPC. Bail still follows the maximum term unless the Act says otherwise.
Most offence sections in ss.18–29 and 36–39 state that the offence is an arrestable offence (e.g. s.18(5), s.26(4), s.36(4)). Check the specific section; others follow the CPC term default.
Any police officer may arrest without warrant any person offending in the officer's view against any provision of the Act, even where the maximum term is under 3 years. Bail is unaffected.
Every offence under the Act is arrestable and non-bailable for the CPC.

A person reasonably suspected of an offence under s.16 or s.17 who refuses or fails to go with a police officer to, or appear before, a Magistrate's Court when required may be arrested without warrant. Other offences follow the CPC term default.
Every offence under s.19 (unlicensed moneylending) or s.47 (harassment) is deemed arrestable and non-bailable. Others follow the CPC term default.
Any police officer may arrest without warrant any person reasonably suspected of committing an offence under the Act.
Several sections carry their own arrest power; s.127 is a qualified power. Otherwise CPC term defaults apply.
Any police officer may arrest without warrant any person offending in the officer's view against any provision of the Act.
CNB or police officers may arrest without warrant a person who has committed or is reasonably suspected of committing an offence under the Act — no in-view limit.
Any police, immigration or customs officer may arrest without warrant any person the officer reasonably believes has committed an offence under the Act or regulations.
No arrest provision found in the Act. CPC term defaults apply.

s.63D: a family violence offence is arrestable for the CPC. s.64E: enforcement officers' power of arrest without warrant. s.174(1): the Director-General, or an authorised police officer (sergeant or above), immigration officer or departmental officer, may arrest a person reasonably believed liable for an offence under ss.140–148 (listed subsections).
